license.notes: Authored 2026-09-16 for Zoo 0.95.0 from the walker's own photographs of 1990s and modern trading-card shops, written up in docs/SET_DRESSING_REFERENCES.md. Construction knowledge only: no brand, no trade dress and no mark from any of them reaches the tools -- every name the species paints comes from core/card_brands.py, which is invented, and a denylist test holds every painted string against the real card games, publishers, graders, leagues, teams and players a writer would reach for.

notes: The strip of angled felt pennants along the top of a shop's wall, overlapping, in many colours. Reference: docs/SET_DRESSING_REFERENCES.md, 'The walker's trading card shop references (2026-09-15)' -- the 1990s sports-card shop it is built to. The colours are `card_brands.TEAMS`, the invented local clubs; NOTHING IS LETTERED, because a pennant at ceiling height is a colour and a band and its ink would be under two pixels. COLLISION: none, and that is deliberate -- a body cannot reach a pennant and a collider up there is a shape the navmesh bake carries for nothing. RANGES: width 1.0 to 14.0 (a long wall); depth 0.06 to 0.12, which is the batten plus two layers of felt; height 0.22 to 0.50, a pennant's drop. BUDGET: 900 triangles, and the pennant count is DERIVED from it -- `pennant_forms.max_pennants` is (budget - 12) // 20, so raising this number is the one dial that makes a strip denser. Measured worst 892.
